voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: Ghent, Belgium. April, nineteen thirty-four. Overnight, a panel of Van Eyck's Ghent Altarpiece vanished from Saint Bavo's Cathedral.
It was called the Just Judges. A second panel, Saint John the Baptist, went with it.
Then came thirteen ransom letters, signed only D, U, A, asking one million Belgian francs.
As proof, Saint John was returned, through luggage storage at Brussels North station. The Just Judges never came back.
More than ninety years on, the case file is still open. A copy hangs in its place.
